items.title: The support of a Borel probability on a separable Banach space has full measure
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a separable real Banach space with its norm metric $d_X(x,x')=\|x-x'\|_X$ and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $X$. Define
$$\operatorname{supp}\mu:=\{x\in X: \mu(U)>0\text{ for every norm-open neighborhood }U\text{ of }x\}.$$
Then $\operatorname{supp}\mu$ is Borel and $\mu(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=1$.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.3 and proof motivate the support-point route; the countable-base/full-measure lemma is proved locally to repair the bounded-noncompact-set shortcut.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used. Separability supplies one countable dense set; the countable families below are explicitly indexed by countable sets, and each later witness is a single local choice.

items.title: Hellinger stability of function-space posteriors under data perturbations
items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be separable real Banach spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be Borel, and let $\mu_0$ be a Borel probability measure on $X$ with $\mu_0(D)=1$. Assume there is a bounded Borel subset $E\subseteq D$ with $\mu_0(E)>0$. Give $D$ the relative norm topology and trace Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(D)=\{D\cap A:A\in\mathcal B(X)\}. Let $R>0$ and let $\Phi:D\times Y\to\mathbb R$ be jointly continuous and measurable from $(D\times Y,\mathcal B(D)\otimes\mathcal B(Y))$ to the Borel sigma-algebra of the extended real line after including its finite real values there. Suppose $M_1,M_2:[0,\infty)^2\to[0,\infty)$ are Borel and nondecreasing in each argument, and for all $u\in D$ and $y,y'\in B_Y(0,R):=\{v\in Y:\|v\|_Y\le R\}$,
$$\Phi(u;y)\ge -M_1(R,\|u\|_X),\qquad |\Phi(u;y)-\Phi(u;y')|\le M_2(R,\|u\|_X)\|y-y'\|_Y.$$
Assume
$$J_R:=\int_D e^{M_1(R,\|u\|_X)}\bigl(1+M_2(R,\|u\|_X)^2\bigr)\,\mu_0(du)<\infty.$$
For each fixed datum $y\in B_Y(0,R)$, define the evidence and posterior by
$$Z(y):=\int_D e^{-\Phi(u;y)}\,\mu_0(du),\qquad \Pi^y(du):=Z(y)^{-1}e^{-\Phi(u;y)}\,\mu_0(du).$$
Then there is $z_R>0$ such that $z_R\le Z(y)\le J_R$ for every $y\in B_Y(0,R)$, and, with the library root-L2 Hellinger distance $h$,
$$h(\Pi^y,\Pi^{y'})\le C_R\|y-y'\|_Y,\qquad C_R:=\frac{\sqrt{J_R}}{2\sqrt{z_R}}+\frac{J_R}{2z_R},$$
for all $y,y'\in B_Y(0,R)$. This is a pointwise fixed-data statement; no observation law or conditional-law version is asserted. In a separate branch, if AC is assumed for the library density/total-variation comparison convention, then
$$\|\Pi^y-\Pi^{y'}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le h(\Pi^y,\Pi^{y'})\le C_R\|y-y'\|_Y,$$
where $\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:=\sup_{A\in\mathcal B(D)}|P(A)-Q(A)|$.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §4.1, Theorems 4.3 and 4.5 and their proofs (PDF pp. 36–39). The local uniform lower evidence bound is proved by a support-point neighborhood; the printed bounded-noncompact-set supremum shortcut is not used. This source uses a 1/sqrt(2) Hellinger normalization; the item uses root-L2 and recomputes constants.

references.title: J. Latz, On the Well-posedness of Bayesian Inverse Problems, SIAM/ASA Journal on Uncertainty Quantification 8 (2020)
references.locator: §3.1, Example 3.1; §3.4, Assumptions 3.5, Theorem 3.6 and Lemma 3.7 with full proof (PDF pp. 7–12 and 24–25). The source proves Hellinger continuity under dominated-likelihood hypotheses, not the stronger IP-17 Lipschitz modulus; it also uses a 1/sqrt(2) Hellinger normalization, so constants are recomputed locally.

items.axiom_use: The Hellinger estimate and pointwise posterior construction are choice-free because the densities relative to the prior are explicit. A separate optional total-variation consequence assumes AC only through the library's generic density/TV comparison convention; that axiom is used only in the final comparison step.

items.title: Hellinger error bound for posterior potential discretization
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a separable real Banach space, let $D\subseteq X$ be Borel, and let $\mu_0$ be a Borel probability measure on $X$ with $\mu_0(D)=1$ and positive mass on some bounded Borel subset of $D$. Give $D$ the relative norm topology and trace Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(D)=\{D\cap A:A\in\mathcal B(X)\}$. Let $\Phi,\Phi_N:D\to\mathbb R$ be finite continuous potentials indexed by integers $N\ge1$, let $M_1,M_2:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be Borel and nondecreasing, and let $\psi_N\ge0$ satisfy $\psi_N\to0$. Suppose for every $u\in D$ and every $N$,
$$\Phi(u)\ge-M_1(\|u\|_X),\qquad \Phi_N(u)\ge-M_1(\|u\|_X),\qquad |\Phi_N(u)-\Phi(u)|\le M_2(\|u\|_X)\psi_N,$$
and
$$J:=\int_D e^{M_1(\|u\|_X)}\bigl(1+M_2(\|u\|_X)^2\bigr)\,\mu_0(du)<\infty.$$
Define the pointwise fixed-data evidences and posterior updates by
$$Z:=\int_D e^{-\Phi(u)}\,\mu_0(du),\quad \Pi(du):=Z^{-1}e^{-\Phi(u)}\mu_0(du),\qquad Z_N:=\int_D e^{-\Phi_N(u)}\,\mu_0(du),\quad \Pi_N(du):=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\Phi_N(u)}\mu_0(du).$$
Then $Z,Z_N$ are positive and finite, and there are $C<\infty$ and $N_0$ such that
$$h(\Pi,\Pi_N)\le C\psi_N\qquad(N\ge N_0),$$
where $h$ is the library root-L2 Hellinger distance. This is a fixed-data assertion and makes no sampling-law or conditional-law version claim. In a separate branch, if AC is assumed for the library density/total-variation comparison convention, then $\|\Pi-\Pi_N\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le h(\Pi,\Pi_N)\le C\psi_N$, where $\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:=\sup_{A\in\mathcal B(D)}|P(A)-Q(A)|$.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §4.2, Theorems 4.8 and 4.9 and their proofs (PDF pp. 40–43). The local positivity proof is replaced by IP-16 propriety plus a normalizer perturbation bound; the printed bounded-noncompact-set supremum shortcut is not used. This source uses a 1/sqrt(2) Hellinger normalization; the item uses root-L2 and recomputes constants.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, M. Dashti, and A. M. Stuart, Approximation of Bayesian Inverse Problems for PDEs
references.locator: §2, Theorems 2.4 and 2.6 with complete proofs (PDF pp. 7–10), and Appendix A, Definition A.2 (PDF pp. 33–34). The paper's Hellinger distance includes a factor 1/sqrt(2); the library root-L2 convention is used here, and the local constant is recomputed.

items.axiom_use: The Hellinger error estimate and fixed-data posterior construction are choice-free because the densities relative to the prior are explicit. A separate optional total-variation consequence assumes AC only through the library's generic density/TV comparison convention; that axiom is used only in the final comparison step.

title: Hellinger stability and posterior discretization — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Equal posterior means do not control the full posterior
items.statement: For any proper prior probability measure on a measurable real-valued parameter space and any two finite likelihood potentials with positive finite evidence and finite posterior means, equality of the two posterior means implies equality of the posterior laws and hence zero Hellinger distance.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §4.1, Remark 4.6: Hellinger control yields expectation control only with second-moment hypotheses.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, M. Dashti, and A. M. Stuart, Approximation of Bayesian Inverse Problems for PDEs
references.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.3: the Hellinger-to-moment direction has explicit moment hypotheses.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used: the prior, likelihood densities, and posterior densities are explicitly given on a three-point space.

items.title: A stable two-point potential gives a Lipschitz posterior
items.statement:
Let $X=Y=\mathbb R$, $D=\{-1,1\}$, and let $\mu_0$ give mass $1/2$ to each point of $D$. For each fixed datum $y\in\mathbb R$, use the finite potential $\Phi(u;y)=\tfrac12(y-u)^2$. Its evidence and posterior mass at $1$ are
$$Z(y)=\tfrac12\left(e^{-(y-1)^2/2}+e^{-(y+1)^2/2}\right)>0,\qquad \Pi^y(\{1\})=\frac{e^{2y}}{1+e^{2y}}.$$
For every $R>0$, this potential satisfies the weighted envelope and data-Lipschitz assumptions of the Hellinger data-stability theorem; hence some $C_R<\infty$ satisfies $h(\Pi^y,\Pi^{y'})\le C_R|y-y'|$ for all $y,y'\in[-R,R]$. These are pointwise fixed-data updates; no observation law or conditional-law version is asserted.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.5 and proof: weighted integrability gives Hellinger Lipschitz stability.

references.title: J. Latz, On the Well-posedness of Bayesian Inverse Problems, SIAM/ASA Journal on Uncertainty Quantification 8 (2020)
references.locator: §3.4, Lemma 3.7 and proof: likelihood continuity gives Hellinger continuity under an integrable dominator.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the prior has two explicitly specified atoms and the posterior densities are explicit.

items.title: A nonintegrable error envelope destroys the linear Hellinger rate
items.statement: For every separable real Banach space $X$, Borel set $D\subseteq X$, and Borel probability $\mu_0$ with $\mu_0(D)=1$ and positive mass on a bounded subset of $D$. Give $D$ the relative norm topology. Let $\Phi,\Phi_N:D\to\mathbb R$ be finite continuous potentials indexed by integers $N\ge1$, let $M_1,M_2:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be Borel and nondecreasing, and let $\psi_N\ge0$ tend to zero. If $\Phi,\Phi_N\ge-M_1(\|u\|_X)$ and $|\Phi_N(u)-\Phi(u)|\le M_2(\|u\|_X)\psi_N$ for every $u,N$, and their evidence normalizers are positive and finite, then there are $C<\infty$ and $N_0$ such that the library root-L2 Hellinger distance satisfies $h(\Pi,\Pi_N)\le C\psi_N$ for every $N\ge N_0$, even without assuming $\int_D e^{M_1(\|u\|_X)}(1+M_2(\|u\|_X)^2)\,d\mu_0<\infty$.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §4.2, Theorem 4.9 and proof (PDF pp. 40–43); its linear rate requires weighted integrability.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, M. Dashti, and A. M. Stuart, Approximation of Bayesian Inverse Problems for PDEs
references.locator: §2, Theorems 2.4 and 2.6 with proofs (PDF pp. 7–10): a linear rate uses an integrable envelope, while a separate compact/tail argument yields convergence without that rate.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used: all parameter values are positive integers and all posterior densities are explicit.
